candidate: exact authoritative theta and C; lookup K
finding: K-only lookup does not retain a meaningful constitutive runtime advantage. Lookup transform/search/reconstruction cost is comparable to or greater than analytical K evaluation for three of four materials.
implication: The next speed candidate should keep theta and C derivative-consistent without evaluating the full analytical retention/capacity pair at every call. A shared interpolant whose derivative supplies C is the preferred next research direction.
nonclaims: K lookup remains numerically admissible as a research representation; this result only rejects it as a speed candidate under the preregistered rule.
